$comment: SINCE PHASE 504 this file is also THE PROOF ROSTER, and the only one: each entry carries a `kind` (`extracted`, `proofOnly`, `generated` or `shared`) and an `opens` list (the registered modules its code references, held to the code by the Proofs.Cone family), and the entries are in CHECK ORDER, every module after what it opens. `check.ps1` reads the modules it hands the kit and the ones it exempts from extraction from here; the Proofs.Ladder family reads the ladder's models, the twin roster and the oracle project's Compile list against it; the cone selector selects from it. A `shared` entry (`Twin`, `ListAlgebra`) is not a model: it is opened by the models, references none, and a change to it puts every module in the cone. What the proof leg COSTS, declared per module, so that a growth in prover time is named rather than discovered when CI times out: every green CHECK line prints the module's measured seconds beside its `budgetSeconds`, and an overshoot is a recorded COST finding, never a red leg. How the leg reads every number in this file — the budget and its both-ways coverage, the cached-read threshold and the `fastestSeconds` that decides whether it applies, the contention factor and its label, the retried abort whose timing is never a cold measurement — is stated ONCE, in the kit engine's header (`proofs/kit/check-proof-leg.ps1`) and its sections 2 and 2b; this file carries the numbers, the rules they were seeded by, and the measurements behind them. Seed nothing from a retried (warm) line or from a run labelled contended. Hand-authored; bumping a number is the recorded act the README's `Running it` section describes. This is NOT `proofs.json`: a wall-clock budget is a claim at none of the ladder's levels, and the ladder's `proof-leg` policy row points here for the cost half. SINCE PHASE 203 each entry also carries `packages`: the packable package(s) whose production code the model is about. That is not a cost fact and it is here for one reason — this file is the only place the model ROSTER is enumerated, so it is the only place a package can be joined to a model without inventing a second roster to drift against. It is read by the `Proofs.Coverage` family (`../tests/Fuaran.Core.Tests/ProofCoverageTests.fs`), whose first clause holds every packable package to either a model named here or an entry in `coverage-exclusions.json`. A name here that is not a packable package fails that clause, so the attribution cannot quietly outlive the package it names.

seeding.rule: budgetSeconds = max(2 x the slowest observed cold-cache run, minimumBudgetSeconds), rounded up to the next 10s.
seeding.$comment: The tolerance is applied ONCE, here, when a number is seeded — `check.ps1` multiplies nothing, so the pair it prints is the measurement against the ceiling and there is no second arithmetic to hold in your head. Seeded from the SLOWEST observed cold run rather than the median, deliberately: on the machine these were measured on, six concurrent sessions inflate a cold check by ~1.8x with nothing about the tree changed (TreeOps 45s to 77s, JsonParse 52s to 99s within one three-run leg), so a budget seeded from the median would fire on a busy afternoon and teach a reader to ignore it. The 20s minimum is for the sub-5s modules, where 2x is inside ordinary process-start noise. These are figures from a Windows dev machine; CI's windows-latest runner is a different machine and its first runs are what will say whether the tolerance is generous enough there. If it is not, that is a bump, and a bump is recorded.

cachedRead.rule: thresholdSeconds = about twice the slowest CACHED read measured on the pinned prover; appliesFromFastestSeconds = three times the threshold. A module whose recorded fastestSeconds is at or above appliesFromFastestSeconds and whose cold check finishes under thresholdSeconds FAILS the leg as a probable cached read; a module below it rests on the cache provenance check alone.

Ten modules were cold-checked in roster order into one fresh cache, as the leg does, and then each was re-run three times against the populated cache with the leg's own flags. WARM (cached) reads: DagFold 0.44/0.34/0.34s, WireDecode 0.24/0.24/0.23s, TreeOps 0.43/0.43/0.44s, Skeleton 0.43/0.44/0.46s, Chain 0.28/0.28/0.32s, JsonParse 0.23/0.25/0.24s, Preservation 0.51/0.49/0.51s, Limits 0.18/0.18/0.18s, Utf8 0.20/0.18/0.20s, WireCanon 0.38/0.38/0.37s: 0.18s to 0.51s whatever the module costs cold. The same modules' COLD checks in that pass: 75.1s, 36.1s, 83.1s, 1.61s, 39.9s, 146.4s, 77.3s, 0.38s, 29.8s and 184.0s. Every cold check printed at least three Quake query lines and every warm read printed none.
cachedRead.$comment: What the threshold is for, and why one absolute number serves every module, is stated once in the kit engine's header (`proofs/kit/check-proof-leg.ps1`, step 1: the clock is a gate in one direction only). THIS repository's seeding: `measured` above is the record; a cached read cost 0.2-0.5s for a 1s module and a 184s module alike, so the threshold is about twice the slowest, and the threefold margin to `appliesFromFastestSeconds` covers a machine roughly twice as fast as the one measured, which is what the Linux runner measured. Modules that can genuinely check in about a second (recorded fastestSeconds under 3) are not judged by it and rest on the cache provenance check alone. Re-seeding is a recorded act: new measurements, the numbers, your phase. A cached read prints no `Quake:` line where every measured cold check printed at least three; whether that becomes a second, timing-free discriminator is the operator decision DECISIONS.md D131 records.

contentionSeeding.rule: threshold = a number above the median ratio of a measured QUIET pass on the SLOWEST machine that runs this leg, and at or below the median ratio of the contention worth naming. Place it high: a false label suppresses a real regression, where a missed label costs only what the leg did before.
contentionSeeding.$comment: What the contention factor is, what a label does to a cost finding, why the factor's neutral point sits well BELOW one, and what `minimumSamples`, `minimumSeconds` and an entry's optional `contentionFactor` mean, is stated once in the kit engine's header (`proofs/kit/check-proof-leg.ps1`, THE CONTENTION FACTOR and WHAT THE NUMBER'S SCALE ACTUALLY IS) and its section 2b. THIS repository's seeding: a quiet cold pass of the whole leg on the dev machine measured x0.29 over sixteen contributing modules (DagFold 14s, WireDecode 9s, TreeOps 19s, Chain 4s, JsonParse 19s, Preservation 13s, TreeDiff 4s, WireCanon 9s, Vocabulary 3s, VocabularyProofs 5s, DocVocabulary 4s, DocVocabularyProofs 7s, ScoreVocabulary 7s, ScoreVocabularyProofs 14s, ColumnOps 12s, Capability 6s; machine idle), and the same leg under four sustained competing provers x0.40 (every large module 1.4-1.7x its quiet time). The incidents the threshold exists to name — Chain's 35s/31s against 30s, TreeOps at 145s, Capability at 75s against 20s — all ran beside six concurrent sessions, the load `measuredSeconds` was seeded under, so they sit near x1.0 by construction. 0.8 sits between: a machine up to 2.7x slower than the quiet pass still reads an ordinary pass as ordinary, and four bare competing provers (x0.40) are deliberately NOT labelled, because a false label is the expensive error. Open: CI's windows-latest runner is a slower machine, and its quiet pass is what will say whether 0.8 clears it; a re-seed records the new number, the quiet factor it came from and the phase. `minimumSeconds` excludes Skeleton, Limits and WireVersioning here.
